cards.text: Jerusalem has been warned that disaster is coming from the north (Jeremiah 6:1). Now the LORD says, “Stand at the crossroads and look.” Picture a traveler stopped where the roads split, deciding which way to go.

cards.question: Standing at the crossroads, the people are told to ask for the ancient paths. What question should they ask?

cards.text: Then the LORD gives the promise: “Then walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.” Friend, I spent years lying perfectly still in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, that was NOT rest.

cards.question: True or false: The people agree to walk in the good way the LORD points them to.

cards.text: Their answer: “We will not walk in it!” The LORD also says He appointed watchmen over them and told them, “Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn.”

cards.question: The ram’s horn is the warning signal. When the people are told to listen for it, what do they answer?

cards.text: So the LORD calls out for others to hear and learn what will happen to this people.

cards.question: Who does the LORD call on to hear what will happen to this people?

answers.text: The nations and the whole earth

cards.question: The LORD says He is bringing disaster on this people. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They bowed down to other gods

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, “What use to Me is frankincense from Sheba or sweet cane from a distant land?” Sheba is a land in Arabia, and friend, that is a LONG way to haul anything.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says the people’s sacrifices do not please Him.

cards.text: Therefore the LORD says He will lay stumbling blocks before this people. You know that dark living room at night, when your FEET find every single thing on the floor?

cards.question: Fathers and sons alike will be staggered by these stumbling blocks. What does the LORD say will happen to friends and neighbors?

cards.text: Then the LORD says to look: an army is coming from the land of the north. It's a great nation, stirred up from the ends of the earth.

cards.question: This army from the north grasps the bow and spear. How does the LORD describe them?

cards.text: Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, lined up like men in formation against the Daughter of Zion. Friend, ONE horse looks at me funny and I'm diving face-first into the chocolate chips.

cards.question: True or false: When the report about this army is heard, everyone gets ready to fight.

cards.text: Then comes the cry: “We have heard the report; our hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped us, pain like that of a woman in labor.”

cards.question: The enemy has a sword, and terror is on every side. True or false: The warning says not to go out to the fields or walk the road.
Then comes the call: “O daughter of my people, dress yourselves in sackcloth and roll in ashes.” They are to mourn as they would for an only son. Why mourn like that?

cards.text: Then the LORD hands out a job: “I have appointed you to examine My people like ore, so you may know and try their ways.” That's me breaking one cookie open to see what a batch is REALLY like inside.

cards.question: The LORD says His people are all hardened ___, walking around as slanderers.

cards.text: They are bronze and iron, and all of them are corrupt. Then the picture turns to a furnace: the bellows blow fiercely, blasting away the lead with fire.

cards.question: True or false: The refining fire purges the wicked out of the people.

cards.text: The refining proceeds in vain, for the wicked are not purged. All that heat, and nothing comes out clean.

cards.question: At the end of the furnace picture, what does the LORD say His people are called?

cards.text: And the reason is the hardest line of all: the LORD has rejected them. I think this one hurts, friend.
